questions.question: When and where was the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) adopted?
questions.explanation: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly in Paris on December 10, 1948 — now Human Rights Day.

questions.question: Who chaired the committee that drafted the UDHR?
questions.explanation: The drafting committee was chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt.

questions.question: How many articles does the UDHR contain?
questions.explanation: The UDHR consists of a preamble and 30 articles setting out fundamental rights and freedoms.

questions.question: Which characteristic means UDHR rights cannot be taken away or surrendered?
questions.explanation: The UDHR describes rights as universal, indivisible, inalienable (cannot be taken away) and non-discriminatory.

questions.question: Which two legally binding treaties, with the UDHR, form the International Bill of Human Rights?
options: The Rio Declaration and the Paris Agreement
questions.explanation: The International Bill of Human Rights consists of the UDHR plus the legally binding ICCPR and ICESCR (both 1966).
